movement_source: row 'Net profit after tax from continuing operations - cash basis', column FY25 (12 months ended Jun 25) -> column FY26 (12 months ended Jun 26)
headline: Cash NPAT (continuing operations) rose $730m or 7.1% to $10,982m in FY26 from $10,252m in FY25. Statutory NPAT rose $750m to $10,866m (continuing operations +$778m to $10,911m); the gap is non-cash items - hedging/IFRS volatility and disposal gains/losses/transaction costs. Growth was driven by NII +$1,563m on 8% AIEA growth partly offset by NIM -3bps, and other operating income +$196m, offset by underlying opex +$719m, notable items +$40m, impairment +$62m and tax +$208m.

drivers.narrative: NII up $1,563m or 7% to $25,586m. Driven by an $92bn or 8% rise in average interest earning assets to $1,246bn, partly offset by a 3bps NIM decline to 2.05%. Volume and margin are not separately quantified in dollars, so claimed as total NII.
Up $196m or 4% to $4,638m: commissions +$135m, lending fees +$12m, funds management +$12m, other income +$46m, partly offset by trading income -$9m.

drivers.columns: FY25 (12 months ended Jun 25) -> FY26 (12 months ended Jun 26)
drivers.narrative: UNDERLYING operating expenses (ex-notables) rose $719m or 5.6% from $12,866m to $13,585m: staff +$288m, IT +$393m, other +$57m, occupancy -$19m. Expense increase is a negative contribution to cash earnings.

drivers.columns: FY25 (12 months ended Jun 25) -> FY26 (12 months ended Jun 26)
drivers.narrative: Restructuring and notable items rose from $130m in FY25 to $170m in FY26, a $40m larger charge and thus a negative $40m contribution. Stated separately from underlying expenses per the bank's own split.
LIE up $62m or 9% to $788m; loss rate up 1bp to 8bps of average GLAAs. RBS +$106m and NZ +$11m, partly offset by Business Banking -$45m and IB&M -$16m. Higher charge is a negative contribution.
Corporate tax expense up $208m or 5% to $4,699m, reflecting a 30.0% effective tax rate (down 50bps from 30.5%, on lower non-deductible expenses). Higher tax is a negative contribution.

notable_items: Restructuring and notable items were $170m in FY26 vs $130m in FY25 (ev-17, ev-45); the $40m delta is claimed as its own notable_items driver.

Statutory-to-cash reconciliation items are NOT bridge drivers: FY26 non-cash items were -$71m continuing (transaction costs/disposals -$17m, hedging/IFRS volatility -$54m) vs -$119m in FY25 (ev-46, ev-78, ev-79, ev-44).
H2 FY26 tax benefited from a one-off finalisation of tax matters (ev-36) - a half-on-half observation, not a FY26 vs FY25 driver.

disagreements.explanation: Slide 7 (ev-57, ev-58, ev-60) appears to shift year labels by one: it prints operating income FY25 30,224 / FY26 28,465, the reverse of the profit announcement's FY26 30,224 / FY25 28,465 (ev-45). The profit announcement table wins per the source hierarchy.
Slide 24 shows FY25 notable items as 0, inconsistent with the profit announcement's $130m; the results book table is primary.

disagreements.topic: Other operating income vs trading income labels
values: Other operating income 4,638 FY26 / 4,442 FY25 - profit announcement (ev-1)
Other operating income 1,199 / 1,190 and trading income 4,442 / 4,638 - results presentation slide 64 (ev-75, ev-76)
disagreements.explanation: Slide 64 appears to swap the labels: 1,190/1,199 are the trading income figures and 4,442/4,638 the other operating income figures per the profit announcement (ev-1, ev-4).
Slide 24 prints a computed unrounded figure; the profit announcement's rounded 12,866 is primary.
Slide 24's FY25 operating performance does not reconcile with its own income and expense figures; the profit announcement summary table is primary.

limitations: NII volume and margin effects are not separately quantified in dollars; the $1,563m is claimed as total NII per the taxonomy, with AIEA +$92bn and NIM -3bps as unquantified narrative context.

The bridge is on a continuing-operations cash basis. Discontinued-operations cash NPAT was $1m in FY25 and nil in FY26 (ev-46), a -$1m effect excluded from the +$730m movement; total cash NPAT including discontinued moved +$729m.

No walk charts were extracted, so no bar-level walk validation was possible; the bridge was built from stated movements and table-level deltas, and it sums exactly to the +$730m movement with zero residual.

Underlying operating expenses and notable items deltas were computed from period levels (confidence capped at 80); NII, other operating income, impairment and tax movements were stated by the bank against the prior comparative period.
Several presentation slides carry year-label or label errors (see disagreements); all driver figures are taken from the profit announcement per the source hierarchy.
Expenses are claimed on the underlying/notable split; the bank equally publishes the combined headline framing, so both claims are capped at 80.
